looks_like_me_why: Bald head, beard and smile are definitely me. Pages 0, 1 and 9–10 are the most recognizable. It's stylized though — big cartoon eyes and exaggerated expressions on some close-ups (pages 6, 16, 17) make it feel less like my real face. Page 20 with the final family shot still reads like me to my boys, which is what matters most.
rings_true_why: Solid, faithful Jack and the Beanstalk. Text is simple and kid-friendly. Images hit the classic beats — sell the cow, magic beans, beanstalk, castle, hen, harp, chase, chop. Feels like a real children's picture book.
professional_why: Looks like studio-level art. Consistent style, great color and composition. Layout and pacing feel polished. I would print it and gift it. I'd pay 99¢ to surprise the twins.
not_good: Page 6–7: the beans look like candy/jelly beans instead of mysterious magic beans. Pages 6, 16, 17: facial features get a bit too cartoonish (huge eyes, extra-wide grins) which breaks likeness. Page 20: the kid in the final shot looks like an extra character — slightly confusing who is who. Minor skin-tone/proportion shifts on a few close-ups.
liked: My boys would freak out seeing Dad as the hero. The beanstalk and climbing shots (pages 9–10) are awesome. Colors, lighting and the happy final scene are lovely. Overall very fun and gift-ready.
